source_text: Ναί. ἀλλὰ ἴδωμεν, εἰ ἡ διαθήκη, ἣν ὤμοσεν τοῖς πατράσιν δοῦναι τῷ λαῷ, εἰ δέδωκεν. δέδωκεν: αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἐγένοντο ἄξιοι λαβεῖν διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφήτης: Καὶ ἦν Μωϋσῆς νηστεύων ἐν ὄρει Σινᾶ, τοῦ λαβεῖν τὴν διαθήκην κυρίου πρὸς τὸν λαόν, ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσεράκοντα. καὶ ἔλαβεν Μωϋσῆς παρὰ κυρίου τὰς δύο πλάκας τὰς γεγραμμένας τῷ δακτύλῳ τῆς χειρὸς κυρίου ἐν πνεύματι: καὶ λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς κατέφερεν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν δοῦναι. καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς Μωϋσῆν. Μωϋσῆ Μωϋσῆ, κατάβηθι τὸ τάχος, ὅτι ὁ λαός σου, ὃν ἐξήγαγες ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου. ἠνόμησεν. καὶ συνῆκεν Μωϋσῆς, ὅτι ἐποίησαν ἑαυτοῖς πάλιν χωνεύματα, καὶ ἔρριψεν ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν, καὶ συνετρίβησαν αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης κυρίου. Μωϋσῆς μὲν ἔλαβεν, αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἐγένοντο ἄξιοι. πῶς δὲ ἡμεῖς ἐλάβομεν, μάθετε. Μωϋσῆς θεράπων ὢν ἔλαβεν, αὐτὸς δὲ κύριος ἡμῖν ἔδωκεν εἰς λαὸν κληρονομίας, δἰ ἡμᾶς ὑπομείνας. ἐφανερώθη δέ. ἵνα κἀκεῖνοι τελειωθῶσιν τοῖς ἁμαρτήμασιν, καὶ ἡμεῖς διὰ τοῦ κληρονομοῦντος διαθήκην κυρίου Ἰησοῦ λάβωμεν, ὃς εἰς τοῦτο ἡτοιμάσθη, ἵνα αὐτὸς φανείς, τὰς ἤδη δεδαπανημένας ἡμῶν καρδίας τῷ θανάτῳ καὶ παραδεδομένας τῇ τῆς πλάνης ἀνομίᾳ λυτρωσάμενος ἐκ τοῦ σκότους, διάθηται ἐν ἡμῖν διαθήκην λόγῳ. γέγραπται γάρ, πῶς αὐτῷ ὁ πατὴρ ἐντέλλεται, λυτρωσάμενον ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ σκότους ἑτοιμάσαι ἑαυτῷ λαὸν ἅγιον. λέγει οὖν ὁ προφήτης: Ἐγὼ κύριος, ὁ θεός σου, ἐκάλεσά σε ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ κρατήσω τῆς χειρός σου καὶ ἐνισχύσω σε, καὶ ἔδωκά σε εἰς διαθήκην γένους, εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς τυφλῶν καὶ ἐξαγαγεῖν ἐκ δεσμῶν πεπεδημένους καὶ ἐξ οἴκου φυλακῆς καθημένους ἐν σκότει. γινώσκομεν οὖν, πόθεν ἐλυτρώθημεν. πάλιν ὁ προφήτης λέγει: Ἰδού, τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν, τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς, οὕτως λέγει κύριος ὁ λυτρωσάμενός σε θεός. καὶ πάλιν ὁ προφήτης λέγει: Πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπ’ ἐμέ, οὖ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι ταπεινοῖς χάριν, ἀπέσταλκέν με ἰάσασθαι τοὺς συντετριμμένους τὴν καρδίαν, κηρῦξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, καλέσαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτὸν καὶ ἡμέραν ἀνταποδόσεως, παρακαλέσαι πάντας τοὺς πενθοῦντας.
pass_a_gloss: Yes, but let us see if the covenant, which He swore to give to the people, He gave; He gave, but they themselves were not worthy to receive because of their sins. For the prophet says: And Moses was fasting on Mount Sinai, to receive the covenant of the Lord for the people, for forty days and forty nights. And Moses received from the Lord the two tablets written with the finger of the Lord's hand in spirit; and having received, Moses brought them down to the people to give. And the Lord said to Moses: Moses, Moses, come down quickly, because your people, whom you led out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly. And Moses understood that they had made for themselves molten idols again, and he threw them out of his hands, and the tablets of the Lord's covenant were shattered. Moses received, but they themselves were not worthy. How then did we receive? Learn. Moses, being a servant, received, but the Lord Himself gave to us, to a people of inheritance, having endured for our sake. He was revealed so that they might be completed in their sins, and we, through the heir of the Lord's covenant, Jesus, might receive, who was prepared for this, that having appeared, He might redeem our hearts, which had already been spent on death and handed over to the lawlessness of error, from darkness, and might covenant with us in word. For it is written how the Father commands Him, having redeemed us from darkness, to prepare for Himself a holy people. The prophet says: I am the Lord your God, who called you in righteousness and will hold your hand and strengthen you, and I gave you as a covenant to the nation, to be a light to the nations, to open the eyes of the blind and to lead out those bound in chains and sitting in prison in darkness. We know, then, from where we were redeemed. Again, the prophet says: Behold, I have set you as a light to the nations, to be for salvation to the end of the earth, thus says the Lord who redeemed you, God. And again the prophet says: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, He sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to call the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of recompense, to comfort all who mourn.

bible_refs.note: I am the Lord your God, who called you in righteousness
I have set you as a light to the nations
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor

pass_b_english: Yes, but let us see whether the covenant God swore to give the people was actually given. It was given, but the people themselves were not worthy to receive it because of their sins. The prophet says that Moses fasted on Mount Sinai for forty days and forty nights to receive the Lord's covenant for the people. Moses received the two tablets, written by the finger of the Lord's own hand in the Spirit, and brought them down to give to the people. Then the Lord said to Moses, "Moses, Moses, come down quickly, because your people, whom you led out of Egypt, have acted lawlessly" (Exod 32:7). Moses understood they had made molten idols for themselves again, so he threw the tablets from his hands and they shattered. Moses received the covenant, but the people proved unworthy.

So how did we receive it? Learn this: Moses received it as a servant, but the Lord Himself gave it to us as a people of inheritance, having endured suffering for our sake. He was revealed so that they might be completed in their sins, and so that we, through the heir of the Lord's covenant, Jesus, might receive it. He was prepared for this very purpose: that by appearing He might redeem our hearts—hearts already spent on death and handed over to the lawlessness of error—from darkness, and might establish a covenant with us in word. Scripture says this is how the Father commands Him: having redeemed us from darkness, He is to prepare a holy people for Himself (Isaiah 42:6-7). The prophet declares, "I am the Lord your God; I called you in righteousness, I will hold your hand and strengthen you. I gave you as a covenant to the nation, a light to the nations, to open blind eyes and bring out those bound in chains from prison, those sitting in darkness."

We know, then, from what we were redeemed. Again the prophet says: "Behold, I have set you as a light to the nations, to be salvation to the end of the earth," says the Lord who redeemed you, God (Isaiah 49:6). And again the prophet says: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me to preach good news to the poor; He sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of recompense, to comfort all who mourn" (Isaiah 61:1-2).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering with appropriate scripture citations (Exod 32:7, Isaiah 42:6-7, Isaiah 49:6, Isaiah 61:1-2) that match the quoted content. All clauses, including the complex description of Jesus's mission and the prophetic quotations, are preserved.
